case.question: How many times can I retry a failed payment request?

result.answer: Demo evidence excerpt: # ExamplePay integration handbook (fictional) ## Retries Retry failed payment requests at most three times. Use exponential backoff with delays of 1, 2, and 4 seconds. Retry only HTTP 429 and HTTP 503. Never retry HTTP 400 or HTTP 401 without correcting the request. ## Idempotency Send an Idempotency-Key header on every payment creation request. Reuse the same key when retrying the same payment. Keys expire after 24 hours. A new key can create a second payment. ## Timeouts The payment request timeout is 10 seconds. A timeout does not prove the payment failed. Check the payment status before attempting another payment.

# ExamplePay webhooks (fictional) ## Delivery Webhook delivery uses HTTPS POST requests. Return HTTP 200 within five seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failed webhook deliveries are retried up to eight times over 24 hours. ## Verification Verify the X-ExamplePay-Signature header using the webhook signing secret and the raw request body. Reject timestamps older than five minutes to reduce replay attacks. The signing secret differs from your API token. ## Deduplication Each webhook has an event_id. Store processed event identifiers and ignore duplicate events. Delivery order is not guaranteed; fetch the current payment state when event order matters.

# ExamplePay authentication (fictional) ## Requests Authenticate API requests with an Authorization header containing Bearer followed by your API token. Create tokens in the developer dashboard. Keep tokens on the server and never include them in browser code. ## Rotation Rotate API tokens every 90 days. Revoke a compromised token immediately. A revoked token returns HTTP 401 on subsequent requests. The dashboard supports two active tokens so you can rotate without downtime. ## Environments Sandbox tokens start with test_. Production tokens start with live_. Sandbox tokens cannot access production payments. Store tokens in environment variables or a secret manager.

retrieved_passages.text: # ExamplePay webhooks (fictional) ## Delivery Webhook delivery uses HTTPS POST requests. Return HTTP 200 within five seconds to acknowledge delivery. Failed webhook deliveries are retried up to eight times over 24 hours. ## Verification Verify the X-ExamplePay-Signature header using the webhook signing secret and the raw request body. Reject timestamps older than five minutes to reduce replay attacks. The signing secret differs from your API token. ## Deduplication Each webhook has an event_id. Store processed event identifiers and ignore duplicate events. Delivery order is not guaranteed; fetch the current payment state when event order matters.

# ExamplePay integration handbook (fictional) ## Retries Retry failed payment requests at most three times. Use exponential backoff with delays of 1, 2, and 4 seconds. Retry only HTTP 429 and HTTP 503. Never retry HTTP 400 or HTTP 401 without correcting the request. ## Idempotency Send an Idempotency-Key header on every payment creation request. Reuse the same key when retrying the same payment. Keys expire after 24 hours. A new key can create a second payment. ## Timeouts The payment request timeout is 10 seconds. A timeout does not prove the payment failed. Check the payment status before attempting another payment.

# ExamplePay authentication (fictional) ## Requests Authenticate API requests with an Authorization header containing Bearer followed by your API token. Create tokens in the developer dashboard. Keep tokens on the server and never include them in browser code. ## Rotation Rotate API tokens every 90 days. Revoke a compromised token immediately. A revoked token returns HTTP 401 on subsequent requests. The dashboard supports two active tokens so you can rotate without downtime. ## Environments Sandbox tokens start with test_. Production tokens start with live_. Sandbox tokens cannot access production payments. Store tokens in environment variables or a secret manager.
